routing_rationale: AI/Education PM — owns Padlet TA and Arcade specifically. The PM-Schools role is currently open and unfilled, making Collin the closest PM to the Arcade-DPA-coverage trigger. Originally flagged as long-shot routing, but research surfaced a Type 1 trigger (his own recent voice on the exact safety architecture). Distinct angle: product-level documentation cadence — the gap between iterating-fast on the safety layer and being-documentable for district vendor assessment.

research_summary.trigger_event: Collin's recent (~March 2026) LinkedIn comment in his own voice, fielding educator safety questions about Arcade: 'We safeguard via prompt on the input side and review with an LLM on the output' + 'we'll improve the LLM review this week.' This is a Type 1 trigger — prospect's own recent statement, on the exact product creating the compliance question.
research_summary.key_insight: Did NOT quote his comment verbatim — paraphrased the architecture in different vocabulary ('two-layer safety architecture', 'pre-generation filtering', 'post-generation review') so the email demonstrates careful reading without echoing his words. Witness flagged v1 opener for being too close to quoting; v2 opened the technical-vocabulary distance further. Did not pitch above his authority (he doesn't sign vendor contracts) — the email's job is to engage with his stated work and start a real exchange about documentation cadence.

draft.body:
The two-layer safety architecture you've been iterating on for Arcade — pre-generation filtering plus post-generation review — is also the architecture a careful district vendor assessment will eventually ask documentation on: which thresholds are stable, which are still moving, and what's been changing week-to-week.

Keeping that documentation in sync with the iteration — surface by surface — is the architectural choice that makes both fast iteration and clean district vendor assessments possible.

Transilience keeps that documentation layer in step with what's deployed — even with weekly iteration.

How is the team currently handling Arcade safety documentation?
draft.architecture: signal-to-question — paraphrases his stated architecture in different vocabulary, names the documentation-cadence question that follows, one product sentence (concrete: 'in step with what's deployed'), one open question CTA

verdict_history.reason: Opener paraphrased too close to his LinkedIn words ('prompt safeguards on input, LLM review on output'); preempt-pivot template structure in middle sentence; CTA was rhetorical with only one honest answer; wh-cleft 'Where Transilience sits is' echoed Nitesh's wh-cleft.

Subject 'The documentation gap behind Arcade safety' named a deficit + 'gap' echoed Audrey's draft. Transilience sentence too dense ('attestation surface / product surface' parallel too abstract). CTA trailing 'as the iteration pace continues' was a leading nudge.

Subject reset to flat-technical 'Arcade safety documentation cadence' — no deficit, no 'gap'. Transilience sentence concrete and short ('in step with what's deployed'). CTA stripped to single open question.

witness.what_works: Opener paraphrases his stated architecture in different technical vocabulary — demonstrates careful reading without verbatim quoting. Subject is flat technical, no deficit-naming. Product sentence is the shortest of the four Padlet drafts (17 words), concrete object ('what's deployed'). CTA is genuinely open, doesn't pre-judge.
witness.what_fails: The opener is the longest sentence in the email and densely loaded — three concrete details (architecture pieces, district vendor assessment, three documentation-question shapes). A scanning reader could bail before the second paragraph. Acceptable because Collin is the lead with the strongest individual trigger (his own recent LinkedIn voice on the exact topic) — the email earns the reader's attention on substance.
